# Pay app guides: schedule of values calculator and pay application guides

> Free, private schedule of values / continuation sheet calculator for construction subcontractors (work completed, stored materials, retainage held and released, balance to finish, current payment due), plus plain-English guides on filling out a pay application, retainage with cited public retainage caps for 16 US states, conditional vs unconditional lien waivers, and change orders, plus a change order log. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Not legal, tax, accounting or financial advice. Not affiliated with the American Institute of Architects and does not reproduce the AIA G702/G703 forms. Statutes were read on 2026-11-24; check the linked statute before relying on it. PayApps, hosted pay-app billing for subcontractors, is open: pay applications with retainage and change orders, free on one active job with no card, at https://payapps.marisstella.app/?signup . Lien waivers, QuickBooks and job costing are in paid plans, which are not on sale yet.

## Pages

- [Schedule of values calculator](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/): continuation-sheet arithmetic, over-billing check, summary, CSV.
- [How to fill out a pay application](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/how-to-fill-out-a-pay-application.html): every column and summary line with a worked example, what to attach, and how to send the backup as one PDF (and the HEIC photos, locked PDFs and spreadsheets that get in the way).
- [Retainage explained](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-explained.html): calculation, reduction, release, lines with their own rate or none (bond lines), flow-down, and public retainage caps for CA, TX, FL, NY, PA, IL, NC, MI, VA, WA, MA, AZ, MN, NV, OR, UT with official statute links.
- [Conditional vs unconditional lien waivers](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/conditional-vs-unconditional-lien-waivers.html): the four waiver types, when to sign each, California and Florida statutory forms.
- [Free schedule of values template (Excel)](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/schedule-of-values-template.html): a blank .xlsx continuation sheet and summary with the formulas in (total completed and stored, percent, balance to finish, per-line retainage, payment due, an over-billing check), plus a filled-in example. No macros or external links; opens in Excel, Google Sheets and LibreOffice.
- [Statutory lien waiver forms by state](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/lien-waiver-forms-by-state.html): which states set the waiver wording by statute (Arizona, Nevada, Texas, Utah, Florida, Michigan, Wyoming, Missouri and California read on the official sites or downloads on 2026-11-25; Massachusetts, c. 254, § 32(4), on 2026-11-26; Georgia, O.C.G.A. § 44-14-366, on 2026-11-26 from the Acts that wrote it, SB 315 of 2020 and SB 143 of 2021; Mississippi, Miss. Code §§ 85-7-419 and 85-7-433, on 2026-11-26 from SB 2622 of 2014, the Act that created them), how many forms, how strictly each must be followed, and the traps in each.
- Statutory lien waiver forms, one page per state, each form printed word for word from the statute with blank lines to fill in by hand and a print button (generated from the same verified text the statute tests check; read 2026-11-25/26): [Arizona](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/arizona-lien-waiver-forms.html), [California](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/california-lien-waiver-forms.html), [Florida](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/florida-lien-waiver-forms.html), [Georgia](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/georgia-lien-waiver-forms.html), [Massachusetts](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/massachusetts-lien-waiver-forms.html), [Michigan](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/michigan-lien-waiver-forms.html), [Mississippi](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/mississippi-lien-waiver-forms.html), [Missouri](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/missouri-lien-waiver-forms.html), [Nevada](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/nevada-lien-waiver-forms.html), [Texas](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/texas-lien-waiver-forms.html), [Utah](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/utah-lien-waiver-forms.html), [Wyoming](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/wyoming-lien-waiver-forms.html). Each page also lists which waiver kinds the state prints no form for, and that state's rules and traps.
- [Change order log](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/change-order-log.html): paste a change order log; revised contract sum, pending money and how long it has waited, billing on unsigned or rejected changes flagged, approved change orders written as schedule-of-values lines for the pay application generator, and exceptions wording for a progress lien waiver; FAQ on following up a change order the GC has not signed.
- [Change orders and the schedule of values](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/change-orders-schedule-of-values.html): approved and deductive change orders on the SOV and summary, and what a change order request to the GC should contain (scope, price by line, contract sum before and after, time, signatures).
- [Retainage in QuickBooks Online](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-in-quickbooks.html): QuickBooks has no retainage field; the Retainage Receivable account and item, the negative invoice line, the release invoice, finding unbilled retainage outside A/R aging, the cash-basis caveat, and an invoice-line calculator. Sources are Intuit help and community pages.
- [Billing in Procore, Textura and GCPay](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/gc-portal-billing.html): how a subcontractor sets up the schedule of values and bills each month in a GC's portal: Procore's Subcontractor SOV CSV import and hand-typed invoice (Work Completed This Period, Materials Presently Stored, New Materials Stored), Textura's This Period and To Date billing uploads, GCPay's three-column SOV upload that must add up to the contract value. A one-line converter and a GCPay SOV check. Sources are the vendors' help pages and a GCPay training guide, read 2026-11-25/26.
- [Prompt payment laws for subcontractors](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/prompt-payment-laws.html): how many days a GC has to pass the owner's payment down to a sub, and late-payment interest, in Texas, California, Illinois, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Virginia (public work) and Florida, each linked to the statute (read 2026-11-25; rates given only where the text read confirmed them), plus a late-payment interest calculator and three follow-up email drafts to send the GC (past due, second request, paid short).
- [Pay application software for subcontractors, compared](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-application-software-compared.html): spreadsheet, QuickBooks Online, Knowify, PayAppHub, Trimble Pay and Siteline with their published prices (read 2026-11-25, aggregator prices marked), what GC portals charge the sub (Textura 0.22% capped at $5,000; Procore Pay 0.2% capped at $4,000 per commitment unless the GC pays; Trimble Pay free when invited), and a portal fee calculator.
- [CoConstruct is closing to new projects](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/coconstruct-alternatives.html): CoConstruct takes no new projects after 31 March 2027 (its migration page, read 2026-11-27; existing projects stay readable); which kind of business should look for a builder suite and which for pay-app billing, a checklist for moving a partly billed job (contract, SOV or draw schedule, approved change orders, billed to date by line, retainage, payments, waivers), and where PayApps fits and does not (no selections, homeowner portal or cost-plus billing).
- [How to get your retainage released](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-release.html): what GCs and owners usually ask for before releasing retainage (punch list, final pay app, final conditional waiver, lower-tier waivers, consent of surety, closeout documents), how the release date is set by the subcontract or a statute, and a release date calculator that writes a dated request letter listing any closeout items still open.
- [Pay application checker](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-application-checker.html): why pay applications get sent back, and a checker that compares this month's draft with last month's approved application line by line: wrong "from previous applications", a scheduled value changed without a change order, a missing line, a new line not numbered as a change order, stored materials that disappeared, a retainage rate change, and previous certificates that are not last month's earned less retainage. Paste CSV or spreadsheet cells; nothing is uploaded.
- [Progress billing for contractors](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/progress-billing.html): draw schedules (milestone billing), percent-complete billing and pay applications compared; how a deposit is credited back on each invoice (spread pro rata, or on the first or last stage) and retainage held on the work; QuickBooks Online progress invoicing from an estimate; and a draw schedule calculator that writes the next progress invoice (this invoice, billed before, billed to date, deposit still to apply, left to bill) and a schedule CSV. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- [Overbilling and underbilling](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/overbilling-underbilling.html): why the percent complete on a pay application and on a cost-to-cost WIP schedule disagree (front-loaded SOV, stored materials, unapproved change orders, cost overruns), what banks and sureties read into each, the adjusting journal entry, and a one-job calculator: earned revenue, over or under billing, gross profit to date, cash against cost, and what to bill next period to finish even.
- [Lien waiver log](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/lien-waiver-log.html): paste the waivers you gave the GC and collected from suppliers and lower-tier subs; conditional matched to unconditional, unconditional waivers given before payment cleared or for more than was paid flagged, paid lower tiers with no unconditional listed, and the next pay app's waivers to request written out. Checks the log against itself; does not decide what a state requires.

- [Pay-if-paid vs pay-when-paid clauses](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-if-paid-clauses.html): paste a subcontract payment clause to see whether its words make it pay-if-paid (owner payment as a condition) or pay-when-paid (owner payment sets the timing), with the phrases that decided it, and how California, Florida, Illinois, Maryland, Missouri, Nevada, New York, North Carolina, Ohio (federal court), South Carolina and Wisconsin treat it, each linked to the statute or court opinion (read 2026-11-25). Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- [Retainage tracker](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-tracker.html): paste one row per job (retainage held and released, completion date, release days from your subcontract, date the release was billed); outstanding retainage, release due dates, aging buckets, overdue days and the carrying cost at your own rate, completed jobs with no release billed, totals by GC, a chase list, CSV. Uses only the release days you enter; runs in the browser.
- [Contractor's sworn statement](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/sworn-statement.html): what Illinois (770 ILCS 60/5, amounts due added by Public Act 103-0827, effective 2025-01-01) and Michigan (MCL 570.1110) ask a sworn statement to list, side by side with official links (read 2026-11-25), and a builder: paste your subs, suppliers and own forces; totals, completed less retainage against paid plus owing, balance to complete, a check that the rows equal your contract sum and the owing column equals this pay request, and the lien waivers to collect. CSV and copyable summary; nothing is uploaded.
- [Miller Act payment bond claims](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/miller-act-payment-bond-claims.html): for subcontractors and suppliers on federal construction jobs. From the last day of labor or material it gives the 90-day written notice date for second-tier claimants (contracted with a subcontractor), the earliest suit date and the one-year limit (40 U.S.C. 3133), says who is not covered (below a sub-subcontractor, J.W. Bateson 1978), whether the contract value needs a payment bond (FAR 28.102-1: above $150,000; alternatives between $35,000 and $150,000), and drafts the notice to the prime. Sources read 2026-11-25. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- [California 20-day preliminary notice](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/california-preliminary-notice.html): for subcontractors and suppliers on private California jobs. Who must get the notice (owner, direct contractor, construction lender if any; none from a laborer; only the lender from a claimant hired by the owner, Cal. Civ. Code § 8200), the last day (20 days after first furnishing work, § 8204), when it counts as given for each delivery method (left and mailed: five days after mailing, § 8116), what a late notice still covers (work from 20 days before it), the contents §§ 8102 and 8202 require, proof of notice (§ 8118), and a printable draft with the NOTICE TO PROPERTY OWNER statement word for word. Statute text from the Legislative Counsel's bulk download, read 2026-11-25. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- [Florida Notice to Owner](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/florida-notice-to-owner.html): for subcontractors, sub-subcontractors and suppliers on private Florida jobs. Who serves it and on whom (the owner; a copy on the contractor from a sub-subcontractor or a supplier to a subcontractor; the notice of commencement's designee; laborers excepted, Fla. Stat. § 713.06(2)), the last day (45 days after first furnishing), the 40-day certified-mail date that makes service count on mailing (§ 713.18(2)), why a late notice loses the lien entirely (§ 713.06(2)(a), (f)), the 90-day claim of lien date (§ 713.08(5)), and a printable draft of the § 713.06(2)(c) form word for word. Statute text from flsenate.gov, read 2026-11-27. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- [Texas lien notice deadlines](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/texas-lien-notice.html): for subcontractors and suppliers at any tier on private Texas jobs whose original contract was signed on or after 2022-01-01 (H.B. 2237). One notice of claim per month of unpaid work, to the owner and the original contractor, due the 15th day of the third month after the month of work (second month on a residential construction project, Tex. Prop. Code § 53.056(a-1)); Saturday, Sunday and holiday extensions under § 53.003(e) shown separately from the date to plan on (holidays from Gov't Code § 662.003); the retainage notice (earlier of 30 days after your contract or the original contract ends, § 53.057(a-1)); the lien affidavit (§ 53.052), its 5-day copies (§ 53.055) and the one-year suit date (§ 53.158(a)); a printable draft of the § 53.056(a-2) or § 53.057(a-2) form word for word, with the § 53.254(g) homestead statement on request. Statute text from statutes.capitol.texas.gov, read 2026-11-27. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- [Paid short: when the GC pays less than the pay application](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/paid-short.html): enter what the application asked for (line 8), the certified amount, each payment received and each deduction the GC named; it splits the shortfall into the certification cut, named backcharges and the unexplained rest, says what to ask about each, lists an unconditional waiver for each payment actually received (never for money not received) and drafts an email to the GC. Plain-language notes on backcharge clauses, held money and closing the balance in the books. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- [When will I get paid? Pay application cash forecast](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-app-cash-forecast.html): enter each job (monthly billing, retainage %, the GC's pay-app cutoff day, days for the owner to pay the GC and for the GC to pay you, months left, optional state) and the applications already sent; it dates each expected payment, lists the late ones, flags a recent cutoff with no application listed, totals money in week by week (late money and retainage kept out of the weeks), and with cash on hand and weekly spending finds the first week the balance goes below zero. Compares GC days with the site's prompt payment table without applying it. CSV and text summary. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- [Billing stored materials](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/stored-materials-billing.html): where stored materials sit on the continuation sheet, the monthly rollforward (stored now = stored last + delivered - installed) that keeps installed material from being billed twice, off-site rules with the federal FAR 52.232-5 text (read 2026-11-25), the backup reviewers ask for, and a rollforward tool that writes the SOV lines and next month's starting sheet.
- [Front-loading a schedule of values](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/front-loading-schedule-of-values.html): what front-loading is, why reviewers reject it and what it costs at the end of a job, and a check: paste the SOV with your estimated cost per line; each line's markup against the job's, value pulled onto early lines, late lines below cost, a balanced SOV, the smallest change that keeps every line within a tolerance, and (with start and finish months) billing, over-billing and job cash by month.
- [Joint checks in construction](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/joint-checks.html): when a GC pays by a check made out to a subcontractor and its supplier, a splitter gives each payee's share (pro rata when suppliers are owed more than the check), what a supplier risks by endorsing with no written split under the joint check rule (Post Bros. v. Yoder, 1977), the waiver each payee signs, a split letter to sign before endorsing, and a joint check agreement checklist; plus which states follow the rule, as summarised in a 2018 surety-industry handout (marked as a secondary source). Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- [Certificates of insurance for subcontractors](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/certificate-of-insurance-for-subcontractors.html): what a GC checks on an ACORD 25 certificate box by box, why the certificate alone does not make anyone an additional insured, the four requests an insurance exhibit usually makes (limits, additional insured for ongoing and completed operations, waiver of subrogation, primary and noncontributory) with the ISO endorsement usually used for each (CG 20 10, CG 20 37, CG 24 04, CG 20 01) and why a certificate is sent back, and how to keep renewals from holding up a pay application. Secondary sources read 2026-11-27.
- [How to write an RFI as a subcontractor](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/how-to-write-an-rfi.html): what goes in a request for information (number, subject, drawing and spec section, one question, a proposed answer, cost or time impact, a needed-by date with a reason), why RFIs get sent back, keeping an RFI log and turning an answer that adds scope into a change order. A drafter in the browser builds the RFI text and checks it.

## Answers

The questions each page answers in its "Common questions" section, with the answer as the page states it. Each link opens that section; the page has the sources.

- [What is a schedule of values?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/#faq): A schedule of values (SOV) splits the contract sum into line items, each with a dollar value. Every pay application bills against those lines, so the owner can see how much of each part of the work is done.
- [How is retainage calculated on a continuation sheet?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/#faq): Retainage is a percentage of the work completed to date, and often of stored materials too, at the rate your contract sets. This page multiplies each line's completed work by the work rate and its stored materials by the stored rate, rounds each line to the cent, adds them, and subtracts any retainage already released.
- [What is balance to finish?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/#faq): Balance to finish is the scheduled value less the total completed and stored to date. Balance to finish including retainage adds back the retainage still held, because that money is also still to be paid.
- [Is this the AIA G702 or G703 form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/#faq): No. The page does the same kind of arithmetic in its own layout. The AIA forms are copyrighted and this page is not affiliated with the American Institute of Architects. If your owner requires the AIA form, copy the numbers into your licensed copy.
- [Does Arizona have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/arizona-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Yes. A.R.S. § 33-1008 sets 4 forms: conditional and unconditional, progress and final. How strict: Unenforceable "unless it follows substantially the following forms". The forms on this page are printed word for word from the statute as read on 2026-11-25.
- [Which Arizona lien waiver form goes with which payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/arizona-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Conditional waiver and release on progress payment: conditional progress waivers. Unconditional waiver and release on progress payment: unconditional progress waivers. Conditional waiver and release on final payment: conditional final waivers. Unconditional waiver and release on final payment: unconditional final waivers.
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver in Arizona?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/arizona-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared your bank. Before that, give the conditional form if Arizona has one, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed amounts out of a progress waiver. This page is not legal advice; ask a Arizona construction attorney before signing anything you are unsure of.
- [Does California have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/california-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Yes. Civ. Code §§ 8132–8138 sets 4 forms: conditional and unconditional, progress and final. How strict: "Null, void, and unenforceable unless it is in substantially the following form". The forms on this page are printed word for word from the statute as read on 2026-11-25.
- [Which California lien waiver form goes with which payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/california-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Conditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment: conditional progress waivers. Unconditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment: unconditional progress waivers. Conditional Waiver and Release on Final Payment: conditional final waivers. Unconditional Waiver and Release on Final Payment: unconditional final waivers.
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver in California?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/california-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared your bank. Before that, give the conditional form if California has one, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed amounts out of a progress waiver. This page is not legal advice; ask a California construction attorney before signing anything you are unsure of.
- [Who has to send a California preliminary notice?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/california-preliminary-notice.html#faq): Before recording a lien claim, giving a stop payment notice or claiming on a payment bond, a claimant gives preliminary notice to the owner, the direct contractor and the construction lender, if any (Cal. Civ. Code § 8200(a)). A laborer does not have to, and a claimant with a direct contract with the owner gives it only to the construction lender, if any (§ 8200(e)).
- [When is the California preliminary notice due?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/california-preliminary-notice.html#faq): Not later than 20 days after you first furnished work on the job (§ 8204(a)). By personal delivery, certified or registered mail, express mail or an overnight carrier the notice is given the day it is delivered or deposited; left and mailed under Code Civ. Proc. § 415.20 it is given five days after mailing (§ 8116).
- [What if I send the preliminary notice late?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/california-preliminary-notice.html#faq): You can still give it, but a lien, stop payment notice or bond claim then covers only work performed within the 20 days before the notice and after (§ 8204(a)). Work before that window is not covered.
- [Is there an official California preliminary notice form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/california-preliminary-notice.html#faq): No. The statute sets the contents, not a form: the names and addresses of the owner, direct contractor and lender, the site, who you are and your relationship to the parties, the work, who hired you, an estimate of the total price, and the NOTICE TO PROPERTY OWNER statement in boldface (§§ 8102, 8202).
- [Does listing the GC as additional insured on the certificate make them one?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/certificate-of-insurance-for-subcontractors.html#faq): No. The ACORD 25 says it is issued for information only and confers no rights on the certificate holder, and that an additional insured needs the policy itself to provide for it or be endorsed. Send the additional insured endorsement page with the certificate.
- [What is the difference between waiver of subrogation and primary and noncontributory?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/certificate-of-insurance-for-subcontractors.html#faq): Primary and noncontributory decides whose policy pays first: yours pays before the GC's own policy and does not ask it to share. Waiver of subrogation decides what your insurer can do after it pays: it gives up the right to recover that payment from the parties named. A subcontract can ask for both, and each usually needs its own endorsement.
- [Can a GC hold my pay application because my certificate expired?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/certificate-of-insurance-for-subcontractors.html#faq): Many subcontracts make current certificates a condition of payment, so check yours. Either way, a lapsed certificate on file is a common reason a pay application stalls, so send the renewal to every GC holding the old one before the expiry date.
- [Who issues the certificate of insurance?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/certificate-of-insurance-for-subcontractors.html#faq): Your insurance agent or broker, the producer named in the top box of the ACORD 25. Ask them for one per GC, with that GC (and anyone else the exhibit names) as certificate holder, and for the endorsement pages the exhibit asks for.
- [What goes in a change order log?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/change-order-log.html#faq): One row per change: its number, a description, its status (pending, approved, rejected or void), the amount, any days of schedule time it asks for, the date it was submitted, the date it was approved, and what has been billed against it.
- [Can I bill a pending change order on my pay application?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/change-order-log.html#faq): Usually not. Most pay applications only carry executed change orders, so pending work is tracked in the log and billed the month it is signed. Some subcontracts allow billing work approved in principle; check yours.
- [How do approved change orders get onto the schedule of values?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/change-order-log.html#faq): Each approved change order becomes its own line, CO-1, CO-2 and so on, with its full amount as the scheduled value; a deductive change order is a negative line. This page writes those lines for you in the columns the free pay application generator reads. Worked example: change orders and the schedule of values.
- [How do I follow up on a change order the GC has not signed?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/change-order-log.html#faq): In writing, to the person who approves change orders on the job (usually the GC's project manager, not the billing contact), restating the number, the scope, the price and any time it asks for, and asking what is needed to sign it. Note the date of each follow-up next to the date submitted, so the log shows how long it has waited and how often you asked. Your subcontract may set how long the GC has to answer, a notice period for claims, or what happens if nobody answers; check it, because this page does not.
- [How do I add a change order to the schedule of values?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/change-orders-schedule-of-values.html#faq): Give each approved change order its own line, CO-1, CO-2 and so on, with its full value as the scheduled value. Do not raise the value of an original line: the original contract sum stays as it was bid.
- [Can I bill a pending change order on my pay application?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/change-orders-schedule-of-values.html#faq): Usually not. A change order request, a pending change order or a signed T&M ticket with no executed change order is usually not billable yet: track it separately and bill it the month it is signed. Some subcontracts allow billing approved-in-principle work, so check yours.
- [How do I bill a deductive change order?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/change-orders-schedule-of-values.html#faq): As a negative line that reduces the contract sum to date. Bill it as completed in the period the credit applies, so the balance to finish on that line reaches zero. Retainage applies to change-order work too, unless the change order says otherwise.
- [When does CoConstruct stop taking new projects?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/coconstruct-alternatives.html#faq): CoConstruct's migration page, read on 27 November 2026, says projects can still be added through 31 March 2027. After that, new projects can no longer be added. Existing projects stay readable, so you can finish active jobs and look back at old ones.
- [Will I lose my CoConstruct project data?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/coconstruct-alternatives.html#faq): CoConstruct says no project data will be lost and that you keep access to see historical project information. Keep your own copy of anything you need for warranty, lien or tax records anyway: contracts, approved change orders, the billing history and payments received.
- [Do I have to move to Buildertrend?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/coconstruct-alternatives.html#faq): No. Buildertrend is the path CoConstruct offers, with a migration specialist and training, but you can choose any software, or split the work between a builder suite and a billing tool. Pick by what your jobs need: selections and a client portal, cost-plus budgets, or fixed-price draw and pay-app billing.
- [Can I move a job that is half billed?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/coconstruct-alternatives.html#faq): Yes, if the new tool can start mid-job. You need the contract sum, the schedule of values or draw schedule, approved change orders, what has been billed to date per line, retainage held and payments received. Finishing the job in CoConstruct is the simpler choice when it ends within a few months.
- [What is the difference between a conditional and an unconditional lien waiver?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/conditional-vs-unconditional-lien-waivers.html#faq): A conditional waiver gives up your lien rights only once the stated payment is received and clears. An unconditional waiver gives them up whether or not you were paid, so sign one only after the money is in your account.
- [Which lien waivers do I send with a monthly pay app?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/conditional-vs-unconditional-lien-waivers.html#faq): A common, safe routine is a conditional progress waiver for this month's amount and an unconditional progress waiver for last month's payment, which has now cleared.
- [What should a progress lien waiver exclude?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/conditional-vs-unconditional-lien-waivers.html#faq): List what you are not waiving: retainage, disputed or unapproved change orders, extra work billed but unpaid, and earlier unpaid progress payments. The waiver should cover work through a stated date and a stated amount, not "all work to date".
- [Does Florida have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/florida-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Yes. Fla. Stat. § 713.20 sets 2 forms: progress and final. How strict: Forms "may" be used, but no one may require a different form. The forms on this page are printed word for word from the statute as read on 2026-11-25.
- [Which Florida lien waiver form goes with which payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/florida-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Waiver and Release of Lien upon Progress Payment: unconditional progress waivers. Waiver and Release of Lien upon Final Payment: unconditional final waivers. Florida's statute has no separate conditional waiver form. Fla. Stat. § 713.20(4) and (5) give one form for a progress payment and one for the final payment, each a waiver and release given in consideration of the payment, with no condition in its text; this page lists those two as the unconditional waivers. § 713.20(7) lets a lienor who signs one in exchange for a check condition it on payment of the check, but the statute gives no wording for that condition, and this page does not supply any. Before signing a Florida waiver ahead of payment, ask counsel.
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver in Florida?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/florida-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared your bank. Before that, give the conditional form if Florida has one, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed amounts out of a progress waiver. This page is not legal advice; ask a Florida construction attorney before signing anything you are unsure of.
- [Who has to send a Florida Notice to Owner?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/florida-notice-to-owner.html#faq): Subcontractors, sub-subcontractors and suppliers who did not contract with the owner. Laborers are excepted, and a contractor who contracted with the owner does not serve one (Fla. Stat. § 713.06(2)(a)). Sub-subcontractors and suppliers to a subcontractor also serve a copy on the contractor, and everyone serves a copy on anyone the notice of commencement names to receive one.
- [What is the deadline for a Florida Notice to Owner?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/florida-notice-to-owner.html#faq): Before you start, or not later than 45 days after you first furnish labor, services or materials, and in any event before the owner's final payment to the contractor after the contractor's final affidavit (§ 713.06(2)(a)). Sent by certified, registered or Global Express Guaranteed mail within 40 days, with a mail log or USPS tracking, it counts as served on the day it is mailed (§ 713.18(2)).
- [What happens if I serve the Notice to Owner late?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/florida-notice-to-owner.html#faq): Florida does not save part of the work the way some states do. Failing to serve the notice, or to serve it on time, is a complete defense to enforcement of the lien by any person, and the time requirements must be strictly complied with (§ 713.06(2)(a), (f)). Small errors in the contents can be forgiven; the date cannot.
- [Is there an official Florida Notice to Owner form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/florida-notice-to-owner.html#faq): Yes. Section 713.06(2)(c) prints the form, and the notice may be in substantially that form but must include its information and its warning. The draft on this page is that form word for word with your details in the blanks.
- [How long do I have to record a claim of lien in Florida?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/florida-notice-to-owner.html#faq): Not later than 90 days after your final furnishing of labor, services or materials (§ 713.08(5)), and the claim of lien must be served on the owner before recording or within 15 days after (§ 713.08(4)(c)). Serving the Notice to Owner does not replace recording the claim of lien.
- [What is a front-loaded schedule of values?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/front-loading-schedule-of-values.html#faq): One where the lines billed early in the job (mobilization, submittals, early rough-in) carry more than their share of the contract's markup, and the lines billed late (testing, closeout, punch list) carry less. The sub collects cash ahead of cost; the owner pays for work before it is done.
- [Is front-loading a schedule of values allowed?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/front-loading-schedule-of-values.html#faq): Contracts rarely ban it by name, but most let the GC, architect or owner's reviewer reject a schedule of values they think is unbalanced, and many cap mobilization. A reviewer who finds front-loading can send the SOV back, rebalance it, or hold the early pay apps. Read your contract's schedule of values and payment articles.
- [How do I check whether my SOV is front-loaded?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/front-loading-schedule-of-values.html#faq): Put your estimated cost next to each line's scheduled value. If every line carries about the same markup on cost as the whole job, the SOV is balanced. Lines well above the job's markup that bill early, and lines below it (or below cost) that bill late, are the front-loading.
- [What is a balanced schedule of values?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/front-loading-schedule-of-values.html#faq): One where each line's scheduled value is its cost times the same factor, the contract sum divided by total cost, so every line carries the same markup and billing tracks cost as the work goes.
- [Can I upload my pay application to Procore?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/gc-portal-billing.html#faq): Not the monthly invoice, as far as Procore's help pages go: they cover exporting an invoice to CSV and importing only the Subcontractor Schedule of Values. The invoice contact types each line's Work Completed This Period and stored materials into the invoice by hand. The SOV detail can be imported from the CSV template the GC downloads from the commitment.
- [How do I upload billing amounts to Textura?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/gc-portal-billing.html#faq): In the billing workflow, open the Progress tab, choose More, then Upload Billing Amounts. Pick This Period Billing Amounts or To Date Billing Amounts, download the template, fill in the billing and retention values, save it as CSV and upload it. Oracle says that if the retention amounts do not meet the draw's retention settings, the system overrides the amounts in the file.
- [Why won't GCPay let me submit my schedule of values?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/gc-portal-billing.html#faq): GCPay's subcontractor guide says the values must add up to the Original Contract Value the general contractor entered, or you cannot submit. Leave change orders out: the GC adds them after the base schedule is approved. The upload takes the GCPay Excel template with three columns: Item Number, Description and Value.
- [What goes in Procore's New Materials Stored column?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/gc-portal-billing.html#faq): Procore asks for the amount of any new materials stored in the current billing period, excluding anything already entered as Work Completed This Period. It only appears when the GC has turned on billing stored materials separately. If your stored balance only rose, the new amount is the rise; if it fell because material was installed, take the new deliveries from your delivery tickets.
- [Does Georgia have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/georgia-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Yes. O.C.G.A. § 44-14-366 sets 2 forms: interim payment and final payment, each waiving "upon the receipt of the sum". How strict: "Shall substantially follow the language of the following form", "in at least 12 point font"; no statement waives lien or bond rights unless it is one of these forms and you have been paid. The forms on this page are printed word for word from the statute as read on 2026-11-26.
- [Which Georgia lien waiver form goes with which payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/georgia-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Waiver and Release of Lien and Payment Bond Rights upon Interim Payment: progress payments, before or after the money clears (the form itself is neither conditional nor unconditional). Waiver and Release of Lien and Payment Bond Rights upon Final Payment: final payments, before or after the money clears (the form itself is neither conditional nor unconditional).
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver in Georgia?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/georgia-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared your bank. Before that, give the conditional form if Georgia has one, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed amounts out of a progress waiver. This page is not legal advice; ask a Georgia construction attorney before signing anything you are unsure of.
- [What does "less previous certificates for payment" mean on a pay app?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/how-to-fill-out-a-pay-application.html#faq): It is the sum of the payment-due amounts certified on earlier applications: not what you were actually paid, and not what you billed.
- [How do I fill in "work completed from previous application"?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/how-to-fill-out-a-pay-application.html#faq): It is the total billed on the line on all earlier applications: last month's total completed and stored for the line minus last month's materials presently stored. Stored material stays in its own column until it is installed.
- [Why do pay applications get rejected?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/how-to-fill-out-a-pay-application.html#faq): Common reasons are a line billed over its scheduled value, "from previous" not matching last month's approved numbers, billing a change order that is not yet signed, retainage at the wrong rate, stored materials without backup, and missing waivers.
- [What is an RFI in construction?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/how-to-write-an-rfi.html#faq): A request for information: a written question to the GC, and through it the architect or engineer, when the drawings or specs conflict, leave something out or cannot be built as shown. The answer becomes part of the job record, so it should be in writing, numbered and dated.
- [Does an RFI answer authorize extra work?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/how-to-write-an-rfi.html#faq): Not by itself, on most subcontracts. An answer that changes your scope, cost or time usually still needs a change order (or a written directive) under your subcontract's changes clause. Price it, send a change order request that names the RFI, and keep the notice deadline in your subcontract.
- [Who should a subcontractor send an RFI to?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/how-to-write-an-rfi.html#faq): Usually the GC's project manager, or whoever your subcontract names, not the architect directly. The GC forwards it to the design team, keeps its own log and sends you the answer.
- [How long should an RFI take to answer?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/how-to-write-an-rfi.html#faq): Your subcontract, the prime contract or the job's procedures may set a response time; read them. Otherwise ask for a date tied to when the work needs the answer, say what is waiting on it, and log the date so a late answer can back a time claim.
- [Should one RFI ask more than one question?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/how-to-write-an-rfi.html#faq): No. One question per RFI gets each answered, tracked and closed on its own. A second question in the same RFI can hold up the first, and a combined answer is harder to cite on a change order.
- [What is a joint check in construction?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/joint-checks.html#faq): A payment from the GC or owner made out to a subcontractor and its supplier or lower-tier sub, so the supplier has to endorse before the money moves. GCs use them so a supplier is not left unpaid and filing a lien for material the GC already paid for.
- [What is the joint check rule?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/joint-checks.html#faq): In states that follow it, a supplier that endorses a joint check with no written split can be treated as paid what it was owed, up to the check amount, even if the sub kept the money. An express or implied agreement of the payer and payees beats the rule, so get the split in writing before anyone endorses.
- [Does endorsing a joint check waive Miller Act bond rights?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/joint-checks.html#faq): Not on its own: the handout this page relies on says the joint check rule does not apply on federal projects with a Miller Act payment bond. A joint check agreement that says endorsement is payment in full can still waive them.
- [Which states have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/lien-waiver-forms-by-state.html#faq): This page covers Arizona, Nevada, Texas, Utah, Florida, Michigan, Wyoming, Georgia, Mississippi, Missouri (unconditional final waivers on residential property only), Massachusetts (a partial waiver and subordination of lien, for those who recorded a notice of contract) and California, each linked to its statute. Statutes change, so open the linked section before relying on a row.
- [Do I have to use my state's exact lien waiver wording?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/lien-waiver-forms-by-state.html#faq): It depends on the state. Arizona, Texas, Michigan and Wyoming ask for the form substantially as written; Nevada's statute makes a waiver unenforceable unless it is in the statutory forms, with no "substantially"; in Florida the forms may be used, but no one may require a different form.
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/lien-waiver-forms-by-state.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared. Send a conditional progress waiver with each pay application, an unconditional one for last month's amount once that payment clears, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed items out of every progress waiver.
- [What is a lien waiver log?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/lien-waiver-log.html#faq): A list of every lien waiver on a job, both the ones you sign for the GC or owner and the ones you collect from your own suppliers and lower-tier subs: who, conditional or unconditional, progress or final, the through date, the amount, when it was signed and when the payment it covers cleared.
- [When is it safe to sign an unconditional lien waiver?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/lien-waiver-log.html#faq): After the payment it covers has actually cleared your bank, and only for the amount you received. Before that, give a conditional waiver, which takes effect only when you are paid.
- [Why collect waivers from my own suppliers?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/lien-waiver-log.html#faq): A supplier or lower-tier sub you paid can still claim a lien on the job until it signs an unconditional waiver for that payment, and most GCs ask for those waivers with your next pay application.
- [Does Massachusetts have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/massachusetts-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Yes. M.G.L. c. 254, § 32(4) sets one form: a partial waiver and subordination of lien, for persons who filed or recorded a notice of contract. How strict: Agreements barring a lien are "void and unenforceable", except this form given "substantially in the following form with no material deviation therefrom". The form on this page is printed word for word from the statute as read on 2026-11-26.
- [Which Massachusetts lien waiver form goes with which payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/massachusetts-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Partial Waiver and Subordination of Lien: A partial (progress) waiver on a Massachusetts job given by a person who has filed or recorded a notice of contract under Mass. Gen. Laws c. 254, § 2. Section 32(4) exempts partial waivers and subordinations of lien given by such persons from § 32's rule that agreements barring lien filing are void, when they are substantially in this form with no material deviation from it..
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver in Massachusetts?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/massachusetts-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared your bank. Before that, give the conditional form if Massachusetts has one, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed amounts out of a progress waiver. This page is not legal advice; ask a Massachusetts construction attorney before signing anything you are unsure of.
- [Does Michigan have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/michigan-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Yes. MCL 570.1115 sets 4 forms: partial and full, conditional and unconditional. How strict: "Shall be used in substantially the following format". The forms on this page are printed word for word from the statute as read on 2026-11-25.
- [Which Michigan lien waiver form goes with which payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/michigan-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Partial Conditional Waiver: conditional progress waivers. Partial Unconditional Waiver: unconditional progress waivers. Full Conditional Waiver: conditional final waivers. Full Unconditional Waiver: unconditional final waivers.
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver in Michigan?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/michigan-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared your bank. Before that, give the conditional form if Michigan has one, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed amounts out of a progress waiver. This page is not legal advice; ask a Michigan construction attorney before signing anything you are unsure of.
- [Who can make a Miller Act payment bond claim?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/miller-act-payment-bond-claims.html#faq): Subcontractors and suppliers who contracted with the prime (first tier), and those who contracted with one of the prime's subcontractors (second tier). Anyone further down has no bond claim: in J.W. Bateson Co. v. United States (1978) the Supreme Court held that "subcontractor" in the Act means one who contracts with the prime.
- [What is the Miller Act 90-day notice?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/miller-act-payment-bond-claims.html#faq): A second-tier claimant must give the prime contractor written notice within 90 days from its last labor or material (40 U.S.C. 3133(b)(2)), by a means that gives written, third-party verification of delivery, such as certified mail with a return receipt. The statute requires no notice from a first-tier claimant.
- [How long do I have to sue on a Miller Act bond?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/miller-act-payment-bond-claims.html#faq): The action must be brought no later than one year after the last labor was performed or material supplied (3133(b)(4)), in the federal district court where the contract was performed. You may sue once you have not been paid in full within 90 days after your last day.
- [Does Mississippi have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/mississippi-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Yes. Miss. Code §§ 85-7-419, 85-7-433 sets 2 forms: interim payment and final payment, each waiving "upon the receipt of the sum", plus an affidavit of nonpayment. How strict: "Shall substantially follow" the form; a form without its NOTICE is "unenforceable and invalid". The forms on this page are printed word for word from the statute as read on 2026-11-26.
- [Which Mississippi lien waiver form goes with which payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/mississippi-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Interim Waiver and Release upon Payment: progress payments, before or after the money clears (the form itself is neither conditional nor unconditional). Waiver and Release upon Final Payment: final payments, before or after the money clears (the form itself is neither conditional nor unconditional).
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver in Mississippi?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/mississippi-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared your bank. Before that, give the conditional form if Mississippi has one, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed amounts out of a progress waiver. This page is not legal advice; ask a Mississippi construction attorney before signing anything you are unsure of.
- [Does Missouri have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/missouri-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Yes. RSMo § 429.016.27 sets one form: unconditional final, residential property only. How strict: On residential real property an unconditional final waiver "shall only be valid if it is on a form that is substantially as follows"; elsewhere no form. The form on this page is printed word for word from the statute as read on 2026-11-25.
- [Which Missouri lien waiver form goes with which payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/missouri-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Unconditional Final Lien Waiver: Residential real property in Missouri as Mo. Rev. Stat. § 429.016.1-.2 define it: new residential construction such as homes of four units or fewer (occupied or not), condominiums, townhouses and cooperatives, and the streets, utilities and common areas on those parcels. Not for repair, remodeling or additions to an owner-occupied home of four units or fewer (§ 429.013), and not for commercial work. On that property an unconditional final waiver is valid only on this form (§ 429.016.27)..
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver in Missouri?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/missouri-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared your bank. Before that, give the conditional form if Missouri has one, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed amounts out of a progress waiver. This page is not legal advice; ask a Missouri construction attorney before signing anything you are unsure of.
- [Does Nevada have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/nevada-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Yes. NRS 108.2457 sets 4 forms: conditional and unconditional, progress and final. How strict: Unenforceable "unless it is in the following forms": no "substantially". The forms on this page are printed word for word from the statute as read on 2026-11-25.
- [Which Nevada lien waiver form goes with which payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/nevada-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Conditional Waiver and Release upon Progress Payment: conditional progress waivers. Unconditional Waiver and Release upon Progress Payment: unconditional progress waivers. Conditional Waiver and Release upon Final Payment: conditional final waivers. Unconditional Waiver and Release upon Final Payment: unconditional final waivers.
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver in Nevada?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/nevada-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared your bank. Before that, give the conditional form if Nevada has one, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed amounts out of a progress waiver. This page is not legal advice; ask a Nevada construction attorney before signing anything you are unsure of.
- [What is overbilling in construction?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/overbilling-underbilling.html#faq): Billing ahead of the work: billed to date is more than earned revenue, where earned revenue is percent complete (cost to date divided by estimated total cost) times the contract sum. On the balance sheet it is a liability, often called billings in excess of costs and estimated earnings.
- [What causes underbilling?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/overbilling-underbilling.html#faq): Most often work on an unapproved change order, whose cost is in the job cost report while the billing waits for a signature. A cost overrun on an estimate that is not updated, a GC cutting your percent complete, and materials charged to the job before they are billed can cause it too.
- [Why do sureties care about overbilling and underbilling?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/overbilling-underbilling.html#faq): A large overbilling means the cash in the bank is partly borrowed from the end of the job. Underbilling is a soft asset that counts profit you have not billed and may never collect; underwriters often discount it, and a pattern of underbillings across jobs is a sign they read as estimates going wrong.
- [Why did the GC pay less than my pay application asked for?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/paid-short.html#faq): Usually one of three causes: the application was certified for less than you applied for, the GC deducted a backcharge, or the GC is holding money without saying why, often for a missing document such as a lien waiver, certificate of insurance, certified payroll or sworn statement.
- [What lien waiver should I sign after a short payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/paid-short.html#faq): One for each payment you actually received, for that amount, once it has cleared. Keep the unpaid balance under a conditional waiver or out of the waiver altogether, and check whether your state fixes the waiver wording by statute.
- [How do I record a short payment in my books?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/paid-short.html#faq): As what it is: a backcharge you accept reduces the job's contract income, a balance you will not collect is a write-off, and a balance you still dispute is a claim you track until it is settled. In QuickBooks that is usually a credit memo against the pay application's invoice; ask your accountant which account it should hit.
- [When will I get paid on a pay application?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-app-cash-forecast.html#faq): Add up the chain: the date you submit (the GC's cutoff day), the days the owner takes to pay the GC after it receives the application, and the days the GC takes to pay you after the owner pays it. A 25th cutoff with 30-day owner terms and a GC that pays 10 days later puts the money about 40 days after the cutoff. Your subcontract, and on some jobs a prompt payment statute, set the GC's part.
- [Why do subcontractors run short of cash on profitable jobs?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-app-cash-forecast.html#faq): Payroll and suppliers are paid every week or two, but pay applications go in once a month and are paid 30 to 60 days later, less retainage. Work done just after a cutoff can wait more than two months to become cash. A week-by-week forecast shows the gap before it arrives.
- [Why do pay applications get sent back?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-application-checker.html#faq): Most often because this month's sheet does not match last month's approved one: a "from previous" column copied from the submitted file instead of the approved one, an edited scheduled value, a new line with no change order behind it, previous certificates typed as last month's payment, or stored materials that vanish or are billed twice.
- [What goes in previous certificates for payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-application-checker.html#faq): Last month's total earned less retainage, which is the amount certified to date. Typing it as what was paid, or as the last payment alone, makes this month's payment due wrong.
- [Can I change a scheduled value on a pay application?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-application-checker.html#faq): Not once the schedule of values is approved. Changes come in as change order lines, and every line stays in the same order and numbering until closeout.
- [How much does pay application software cost?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-application-software-compared.html#faq): Published prices read on 2026-11-25: Knowify Core $99 a month billed yearly or $149 monthly for one user; PayAppHub $39.99, $79.99 and $129.99 a month (an aggregator's figure); a Trimble Pay subcontractor plan listed at $99 a month, and free to submit when a GC invites you. Siteline prices by proposal. Ask the vendor for a current quote.
- [How much does Textura charge a subcontractor?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-application-software-compared.html#faq): Oracle Textura's help pages give 0.22% of the contract value, charged when the contract is confirmed, at most $5,000 for projects created on or after 19 January 2023 ($3,750 before). Lower-tier subs pay a flat $100 per contract. It is a cost to price into your bid.
- [Is a spreadsheet enough for pay applications?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-application-software-compared.html#faq): Under about five pay apps a month, a good spreadsheet is hard to beat. Past that, the time spent retyping previous-period columns and chasing waivers is the real cost, and a broken formula or a stale previous-period column nobody notices is the risk.
- [What is the difference between pay-if-paid and pay-when-paid?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-if-paid-clauses.html#faq): Pay-when-paid sets the time for payment: the GC pays after the owner pays, or within a reasonable time. Pay-if-paid makes the owner's payment a condition, so the sub takes the risk of the owner never paying. Courts look for words like "condition precedent" before reading a clause as pay-if-paid.
- [Is a pay-if-paid clause enforceable?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-if-paid-clauses.html#faq): It depends on the state. North Carolina and South Carolina by statute, and California and New York by their highest courts, will not let the owner's payment be a condition of yours. Illinois, Maryland and Missouri say the clause is no defense to a mechanics lien claim. Whether a clause holds on your job is a question for a construction attorney licensed in the project's state.
- [What wording should I ask for instead of pay-if-paid?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/pay-if-paid-clauses.html#faq): Ask for timing wording with an outside date, such as payment within 7 days after the contractor receives payment and in any event within 45 days after the pay application is approved, and strike "condition precedent" and "assumes the risk".
- [What is progress billing in construction?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/progress-billing.html#faq): Billing a job in parts as the work gets done, instead of one invoice at the end. The parts are set either by stages (a draw schedule: so much at rough-in, so much at drywall) or by how far along each line of a schedule of values is (percent complete), which is how a monthly pay application works.
- [How is a deposit handled on progress invoices?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/progress-billing.html#faq): A deposit is money for work not done yet, so it is credited back against the invoices as the work is billed. The common ways are to spread it over every stage in proportion to its value, or to take it all off the first invoice. Either way, the credits should add up to the deposit by the final invoice.
- [Is progress billing the same as a pay application?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/progress-billing.html#faq): A pay application is one form of progress billing: the percent-complete method written out line by line on a schedule of values, with retainage and the previous certificates, usually monthly. Homeowner and small commercial jobs often use a simpler draw schedule instead.
- [Does QuickBooks Online do progress billing?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/progress-billing.html#faq): Yes, from an accepted estimate, once progress invoicing is switched on in the Sales settings: each invoice bills a percent or an amount of each line, and the estimate keeps track of what is left. It has no retainage field, so retainage needs its own account, item and negative invoice line.
- [How many days does a GC have to pay a subcontractor?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/prompt-payment-laws.html#faq): It depends on the state and often on the contract. In the statutes this page read, Texas, California and North Carolina give the GC 7 days after it receives the owner's payment, Illinois 15 calendar days, and Pennsylvania 14 days after the contractor is paid or after your invoice, whichever is later.
- [Does prompt payment interest stop my lien deadline?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/prompt-payment-laws.html#faq): No. Prompt payment interest does not stop the clock on mechanics lien or bond claim deadlines, so watch those dates at the same time.
- [What should I do first when a GC pays late?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/prompt-payment-laws.html#faq): Find out when the owner paid, since the deadline counts from that date, then put it in writing: name the pay application, the amount, the statute and the interest so far. Several of these laws make suspending work or claiming interest depend on written notice.
- [What is a punch list in construction?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/punch-list.html#faq): The list of small items still to fix or finish near the end of a job, written at a walk-through by the GC, architect, owner or an inspector. Each item is fixed, marked done, then back-checked and accepted by whoever listed it.
- [Who is responsible for punch list items?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/punch-list.html#faq): The trade whose work the item is. An item that is another trade's work, or work built as the drawings show, should be raised with the GC in writing straight away, so it is reassigned instead of staying on your list.
- [Does the punch list hold up retainage?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/punch-list.html#faq): Often. Many subcontracts tie retainage release to completion and acceptance of your scope, and an open punch item is the most common reason given for holding the balance. Your subcontract says what release actually depends on.
- [How is retainage calculated on a pay application?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-explained.html#faq): Retainage held is the work completed to date times the work rate, plus stored materials times the stored rate, minus retainage already released. It is a percentage of everything completed and stored to date, not of this month's bill alone.
- [Can a GC hold more retainage from a sub than the owner holds from the GC?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-explained.html#faq): Several state statutes say the prime contractor cannot hold back a higher percentage from a subcontractor than the owner holds from the prime; California and Texas say so directly. A 10% sub retainage on a 5% public job is worth a question.
- [When is retainage released?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-explained.html#faq): The balance is released at substantial or final completion, usually against a final lien waiver, closeout documents and sometimes a punch list. Many contracts, and some statutes, cut the rate once the job is 50% complete.
- [Does QuickBooks Online track retainage?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-in-quickbooks.html#faq): Not as a built-in field. The usual workaround is a Retainage Receivable account (Other Current Assets, detail type Retainage) and a Retainage item: a negative line holds the money back on each pay app invoice, and a positive line on a later invoice bills it when it is released.
- [How do I bill released retainage in QuickBooks Online?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-in-quickbooks.html#faq): Add the Retainage item as a positive line for the amount released. No new income is booked, because it was booked when the work was billed: the amount moves from Retainage Receivable to accounts receivable, and the customer's payment clears it like any other invoice.
- [Why is retainage missing from my A/R aging report?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-in-quickbooks.html#faq): Because retainage sits in an asset account rather than accounts receivable, the standard A/R aging report does not show it. Open Retainage Receivable from the chart of accounts, or run Transaction Detail by Account filtered to that account, and group by customer and project to see it per job.
- [When is retainage due to a subcontractor?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-release.html#faq): Your subcontract usually ties release to an event (substantial completion of the project, final acceptance, or the GC being paid its own retainage) plus a number of days. A statute may set an outer limit, mostly on public work.
- [What holds up a retainage release?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-release.html#faq): An open punch list item is the most common reason given. A missing final pay application, final conditional lien waiver, lower-tier waivers, consent of surety on bonded jobs, or closeout documents such as warranties, O&M manuals and as-builts can hold it up too.
- [How do I get retainage released sooner?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-release.html#faq): Negotiate the rate and release terms before you sign, bill retainage as its own line, collect closeout documents as you go, and ask in writing on a schedule. Watch your lien and bond claim deadlines while you wait, so they do not pass.
- [How do I track retainage across jobs?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-tracker.html#faq): Keep one row per job with the retainage held to date, the retainage released, the completion date, the number of days your subcontract allows for release after completion, and the date you billed the release. Outstanding retainage is held minus released; the release is due on the completion date plus the release days.
- [Why does my A/R aging report not show retainage?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-tracker.html#faq): Retainage is usually not invoiced until it is released, so in many setups (QuickBooks Online among them) it sits in a separate retainage receivable account and never ages like an open invoice. A retainage tracker ages it from the date the release fell due instead. See retainage in QuickBooks.
- [When is retainage overdue?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/retainage-tracker.html#faq): When the date your subcontract (or, on some public work, a statute) sets for release has passed and it has not been paid. That date is usually a number of days after substantial or final completion, often conditional on closeout documents and a final lien waiver. This page uses the days you enter; it does not decide what your contract or state law says.
- [Where do stored materials go on a pay application?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/stored-materials-billing.html#faq): On the continuation sheet they go in their own column, materials presently stored, which holds material bought for the job and not yet installed. It is added to work completed to give total completed and stored to date, and it is not part of the work-completed columns.
- [What happens to stored materials when they are installed?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/stored-materials-billing.html#faq): The installed value leaves the stored column and is billed as work completed this period. Stored now equals stored on the last pay app plus deliveries this period minus what was installed. If installed material is added to work completed without being taken out of stored, it is billed twice.
- [Can I bill for materials stored off site?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/stored-materials-billing.html#faq): Only if your contract allows it. The federal construction payment clause, FAR 52.232-5, counts off-site material only when the contract specifically authorizes it and the contractor shows evidence of title and that the material will be used on that contract. Private contracts vary; read the payment article of yours.
- [Can I bill my markup on stored materials?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/stored-materials-billing.html#faq): It depends on the contract. Some pay stored material at invoice cost and release the rest of the line's value as it is installed. If yours is silent, ask the GC's project accountant before the first pay app rather than after a rejection.
- [What is a contractor's sworn statement?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/sworn-statement.html#faq): A list of everyone who furnished labor or materials to your part of a job, with what each was contracted for, has been paid and is owed now, signed under oath, usually before a notary, and sent with the pay application. Illinois (770 ILCS 60/5) and Michigan (MCL 570.1110) write it into their lien laws.
- [What happens without a sworn statement in Michigan?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/sworn-statement.html#faq): The lien survives, but a contractor is not entitled to payment, and nobody can file to enforce the lien, until the statement is provided. A false statement made knowingly with intent to defraud is a crime.
- [Does a sworn statement have to add up to my contract?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/sworn-statement.html#faq): Yes. All rows together, including one for your own forces, equal your contract sum, and the owing column together equals what this pay application asks for. For each party, completed to date less retainage equals paid plus owing.
- [When is the Texas notice of claim for unpaid labor or materials due?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/texas-lien-notice.html#faq): On a commercial job, by the 15th day of the third month after the month the labor or materials were provided; on a residential construction project, the 15th day of the second month (Tex. Prop. Code § 53.056(a-1)). Each month of unpaid work has its own date: March work is due 15 June on a commercial job and 15 May on a residential one.
- [Who has to send the Texas notice of claim, and to whom?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/texas-lien-notice.html#faq): Every claimant other than the original contractor: subcontractors and suppliers at any tier on an original contract entered into on or after 1 January 2022. The notice goes to the owner or reputed owner and to the original contractor (§ 53.056(a), (a-1)).
- [What if the Texas notice deadline falls on a weekend or holiday?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/texas-lien-notice.html#faq): Section 53.003(e) extends a deadline that falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday to the next day that is not one. Chapter 53 does not define legal holiday, so this page plans on the unmoved date and shows the extended date separately, counting the national and state holidays of Gov't Code § 662.003.
- [Do I need a separate notice for retainage in Texas?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/texas-lien-notice.html#faq): Yes, for retainage not already included in a monthly notice, if your contract provides for retainage. The notice of claim for unpaid retainage is due by the earlier of the 30th day after your contract is completed, terminated or abandoned, or the 30th day after the original contract is terminated or abandoned (§ 53.057(a), (a-1)).
- [When do I file the Texas lien affidavit?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/texas-lien-notice.html#faq): A subcontractor or supplier files with the county clerk by the 15th day of the fourth month after the month it last provided labor or materials (third month on a residential project), and by the 15th day of the third month after the original contract ended for a retainage lien (§ 53.052(b)-(d)). Send a copy to the owner and the original contractor within five days of filing (§ 53.055).
- [Does Texas have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/texas-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Yes. Prop. Code § 53.284 sets 4 forms: conditional and unconditional, progress and final. How strict: Unenforceable "unless it substantially complies with the applicable form". The forms on this page are printed word for word from the statute as read on 2026-11-25.
- [Which Texas lien waiver form goes with which payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/texas-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Conditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment: conditional progress waivers. Unconditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment: unconditional progress waivers. Conditional Waiver and Release on Final Payment: conditional final waivers. Unconditional Waiver and Release on Final Payment: unconditional final waivers.
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver in Texas?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/texas-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared your bank. Before that, give the conditional form if Texas has one, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed amounts out of a progress waiver. This page is not legal advice; ask a Texas construction attorney before signing anything you are unsure of.
- [Can I bill a T&M ticket on my pay application?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/tm-tickets.html#faq): On most jobs, not until the ticket becomes an executed change order, which then becomes a new line on the schedule of values. Billing a ticket before then is a common reason pay apps get sent back.
- [What should a T&M ticket include?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/tm-tickets.html#faq): The ticket number and date of the work, where and why it was done, each worker or trade with regular and overtime hours apart, material with quantities, equipment with hours or days, and the GC's signature, printed name and date, signed on the day.
- [Does a signed T&M ticket mean the GC agreed to pay?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/tm-tickets.html#faq): Usually not. A signature confirms the time and material were spent; it usually does not agree the price or that the work is extra, so the change order still matters. Whether a ticket counts as written notice of extra work is for your subcontract to decide.
- [Does Utah have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/utah-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Yes. Utah Code § 38-1a-802 sets 2 (conditional progress, final) plus a check endorsement. How strict: Meets the section "if it is in substantially the form provided"; only binds once payment is received. The forms on this page are printed word for word from the statute as read on 2026-11-25.
- [Which Utah lien waiver form goes with which payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/utah-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Utah Conditional Waiver and Release upon Progress Payment: conditional progress waivers. Utah Waiver and Release upon Final Payment: conditional final waivers. Utah's statute has no unconditional waiver form. Utah Code § 38-1a-802(4) gives two forms, one for a progress payment ((4)(b)) and one for a final payment ((4)(c)); each takes effect once the undersigned endorses the check and the check is paid. This package prints those two and does not supply unconditional wording for Utah. If a customer asks for an unconditional waiver on a Utah job, ask counsel.
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver in Utah?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/utah-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared your bank. Before that, give the conditional form if Utah has one, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed amounts out of a progress waiver. This page is not legal advice; ask a Utah construction attorney before signing anything you are unsure of.
- [Does Wyoming have a statutory lien waiver form?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/wyoming-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Yes. W.S. 29-10-101(b) sets one form: a single lien waiver. How strict: "Shall be completed in substantially the following form". The form on this page is printed word for word from the statute as read on 2026-11-25.
- [Which Wyoming lien waiver form goes with which payment?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/wyoming-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Lien Waiver: unconditional progress waivers and unconditional final waivers. Wyoming's statute gives one lien waiver form (Wyo. Stat. § 29-10-101(b)), which waives in consideration of the payment received to date and acknowledges receipt of payment. It has no conditional wording, and this page does not supply any. Before signing a Wyoming waiver ahead of payment, ask counsel.
- [When should I sign an unconditional lien waiver in Wyoming?](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/wyoming-lien-waiver-forms.html#faq): Only once the payment it covers has cleared your bank. Before that, give the conditional form if Wyoming has one, and keep retainage, unapproved change orders and disputed amounts out of a progress waiver. This page is not legal advice; ask a Wyoming construction attorney before signing anything you are unsure of.

## Source

- [Source code and README](https://github.com/duncan-haywood/oss-monorepo/tree/main/ventures/pay-app-guides): FSL-1.1-MIT licensed.
- [T&M ticket log](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/tm-tickets.html): what a time-and-material ticket should show, and a log that prices each ticket at the markups you enter (none assumed), flags unsigned tickets and signed ones still on no change order, writes the pending change order request lines for the change order log, and drafts a change order request listing the figures. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- [Punch list tracker](https://marisstella.app/pay-app-guides/punch-list.html): the columns a punch item should record, and a tracker for the list from the walk-through (a table, or one item per line pasted from the GC's email): open, overdue against the due dates you enter, done awaiting back-check, accepted, or not ours; the retainage you say is held while items are not accepted; a back-check email naming every fixed item; a CSV with a GC initials column. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
